newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK MIXED ON KEY UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK MIXED ON KEY UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted mixed against hard currencies at the close of Friday's interbank session, dealers said.
They said the local unit saw some slight gains on the key U.S. dollar after buckling under import pressure on Thursday, but added that market confidence still remained shaky.
"The confidence isn't there yet in the market. There is still a lot more central (Reserve) bank intervention needed next week to restore full confidence," one dealer commented.

The dealers said the local dollar seemed to have shrugged aside news that the World Bank was set to resume crucial financial aid towards Zimbabwe's economic reform programme which it suspended two years ago citing fiscal indiscipline.
"Our market is not really that sensitive to such news. The transactions we do are really not big enough for that," one dealer said.
The dealers have always maintained that the local foreign exchange market is largely driven by importer demand for currency against export supply more than anything else.

At Friday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 11.7100/7400 against the U.S. dollar compared to Thursday's 11.7200/7400 but was softer on sterling at 18.8500/9000 against 18.5800/6800 the previous day, tracking the U.S. dollar's losses on the British unit overseas.
It was also weaker at 6.4400/4600 from 6.3500/3700 versus the mark but was stable against South Africa's rand at 2.5000/5100.
